Subject: Next steps from today — deployment mode & sizing details

Hi Sara — thanks again for a productive demo call today. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the open items so we can size the right deployment for AcmeAI and make a clean recommendation (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private). Quick recap of what I took away from the call: 

- You prefer Dedicated capacity for production (data isolation + predictable latency) but may move to Private VPC for compliance later.
- Primary workload: realtime chat completions for customer support + short assistants.
- Typical latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for 1–2 turn completions.

Could you confirm the following so our infra team can give an initial GPU pool recommendation? If you have any recent traffic logs or a small sample CSV with request counts that would help but not required.

1) Steady-state TPS (requests/sec) you expect in production vs peak burst (one-hour peak).
2) Typical concurrency per session / number of concurrent users you expect.
3) Average token mix: prompt tokens, generated tokens average per request, and percent of embedding calls.
4) Target model family(s) you are evaluating (we discussed a 13B and a 70B option briefly).

I'll loop Marissa (in cc) for a back-of-envelope capacity estimate once you confirm. Happy to run an official benchmark with your prompt set if you want empirical numbers.

Thanks — Jonas

Thanks Jonas — quick answers below. Copying a couple internal notes so you have context on our end (we'll share a small csv of anonymized traces if that helps).

1) Steady-state: ~200 TPS during business hours (Mon–Fri). Peak: ~500 TPS during major drops/releases (bursts lasting ~30–90 minutes).
2) Concurrency: we typically see 40–80 concurrent active sessions; a single session may issue back-to-back calls but not usually very long chains.
3) Token mix: average prompt tokens ~120, average generated tokens ~80 (so ~200 tokens per call). ~15% of calls are embedding requests (batch embedding jobs happen overnight).
4) Models: starting with a 13B open model for rapid iteration; roadmap could include a 70B variant for higher-quality outputs in Q4.

Notes: low tolerance for sustained latency regressions. We definitely want predictable tail latency and a smooth path to VPC/on‑prem for audits down the line.

Happy to have Marissa or your infra team ask follow-ups.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: AcmeAI sizing info — recommendations (draft)

Jonas / Rishi — quick draft recommendation for AcmeAI based on the numbers below. These are back-of-envelope estimates; propose we offer a 2-hour benchmark with their 200-token-average prompt set to validate.

Summary of Sara's inputs (copied): steady 200 TPS, peak 500 TPS bursts, avg ~200 tokens, concurrency 40–80, starting on 13B, 70B later.

Baseline recommendation (13B model, cost-conscious + predictable latency):
- Pool type: Dedicated A10G-style nodes (cost-efficient for 13B-family models).
- Initial pool size (steady-state): 4–6 A10G GPUs. This should cover ~200 TPS with p95 ~300–450ms depending on batching.
- Burst sizing: autoscale target up to 10 A10G GPUs for short peaks (up to 500 TPS) with aggressive scale-up and graceful scale-down. Use warm-start capacity to reduce cold-start latency.
- Concurrency / batching config: per-GPU max concurrency ~8–12 active callers, dynamic continuous batching with 20–40ms aggregation window. Tune max batch size to match 200-token average.

If they plan to run a 70B family model in prod (higher memory + compute):
- Pool type: prefer A100-80GB or H100 (depending on availability).
- Initial pool sizing: 2–4 x A100 (or 2 x H100) to support an equivalent of ~200 TPS for 70B with higher latency — recommend staged rollout and load testing.

Operational notes & optimizations:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt patterns (can reduce tokens processed and improve p95).
- Use token-based throttles and queueing to protect tail latency during spikes.
- Configure autoscaling policies around request rate and queue length, with conservative cooldowns for scale-down to avoid thrashing.
- Offer to run a 2-hour benchmark using their representative prompt set; we'll deliver a spreadsheet with observed TPS, tokens/s, and estimated GPU-hours and cost.

I attached a draft spreadsheet (dedicated-sizing-estimate.xlsx) and a pool config example (redwood-pool-config-template.yaml) for the MOM.

Next steps to propose to AcmeAI in the follow-up:
1) Share the attachments + short explanation.
2) Schedule a 2‑hour benchmark window (we can run on our side against a snapshot model) — ideally next week.
3) If benchmark matches, propose a Dedicated pilot (30–60 day commit) with autoscale to validate production traffic.

Happy to refine once we have logs or the sample CSV.

—Marissa
